text.p: TORONTO, July 21 Reuter) - The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE GLOBE AND MAIL: Court orders U.S. ferry freed: Fish war intensifies with boat blockade, other anti-Alaska protests by B.C. fisherman
-Karadzic supporters expel President: Plavsic ousted from Bosnian party
-Caution greets IRA ceasefire: Repeat feared of 1994 'farce'
-Milgaard case puts strain on police: Saskatoon department's willingness to pursue 1969 sex slaying questioned
-Mexicans dust off law to stifle media: Old statute allows jailing of reporters
Team lands Prudential properties: Oxford, GE Capital buy insurer's Canadian real estate assets with $450-million-range bid
-Digital moves to soothe investors: Pressure is on for fast improvements
-It's dog-eat-dog in pet food: Grocery stores and independent retailers are fighting to protect their territory against the vet clinics and superstores.
-Bell on the defensive: Sprint Canada's long-distance plan has Bell Canada on the run. It's losing market share and is laying off workers to cut costs
-US$525M deal offers CIBC a window on Wall Street
